title: Priority and Delegation Check
description: NCLEX-style prioritization and delegation questions for entry-level practice.

questions.prompt: Which client should the nurse assess first?

choices.text: A client with COPD whose oxygen saturation dropped from 94% to 88%
A client requesting discharge teaching for insulin administration
A post-op client reporting incisional pain rated 5/10
A client asking for assistance to the bathroom

questions.explanation: An acute drop in oxygen saturation from 94% to 88% in a client with COPD represents a potentially life-threatening change in respiratory status. Airway, breathing, and circulation (ABCs) take priority over education, moderate pain, or ambulation needs.
questions.rationale: NCLEX prioritization questions follow the ABC framework. A six-point drop in SpO2 in a client with underlying lung disease signals acute decompensation that requires immediate nurse assessment and intervention, making this the highest priority.

distractorRationale.B: Discharge education for insulin is important but is not urgent; it can be deferred while the nurse responds to the acute respiratory change.
distractorRationale.C: Pain rated 5/10 requires assessment and intervention, but it is not immediately life-threatening compared to hypoxia in a COPD client.
distractorRationale.D: Assisting to the bathroom is a delegatable task for stable clients and is not a nursing priority over an acute change in cardiorespiratory status.

questions.prompt: Which tasks are appropriate for the nurse to delegate to an experienced assistive personnel? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Obtain routine vital signs on a stable client
Reinforce teaching about a newly prescribed anticoagulant
Transport a stable client to diagnostic imaging

questions.explanation: Assistive personnel (AP) may perform tasks that are routine, non-complex, and require no nursing judgment: vital signs on stable clients, recording I&O, and transporting stable clients. Medication teaching requires nursing licensure and clinical judgment and cannot be delegated to AP.
questions.rationale: The five rights of delegation (right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction/communication, right supervision) govern safe delegation. Tasks involving assessment, teaching, or clinical judgment are reserved for licensed nurses.

distractorRationale.C: Patient education — especially for high-risk medications like anticoagulants — requires clinical judgment, assessment of learning readiness, and licensed nurse accountability. This task cannot be delegated to AP.
